feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed. The only race evidence is iteration 0 (60 trials, 0 finishes, every run ended off track). Progress was 0.24 on the oval, 0.17 on the s-bend and 0.12 on the slalom, with steering_oscillation of 0.10 to 0.14. The candidate's own arithmetic holds: kp 2.5 with weights of +/-2 gives turn up to 5 units, about 1750 PWM of differential, so cutting kp to 1.5 (max turn about 3) directly targets the instability that iteration 0 showed. It is valid against the contract: sensor y = 0.05 is in range, wheel_track 0.14 is in range, kd 0.6 is in range, and the sensor spread and weights are unchanged, so the comparison with iteration 0 is clean. The main risk is that base_speed 1.3 is well below the roughly 1.5 m/s needed to finish in 3 s, and this change is stacked with the kp and kd changes, so the race will not separate their effects. Read the race this way. If runs stay on track and progress rises above about 0.5, keep kp 1.5 and kd 0.6, then raise base_speed in steps toward 1.5 to 1.6 to recover completion time. If runs still leave the track on the slalom while steering_oscillation is high, raise kd further before touching kp. If runs leave the track with low oscillation, the robot is too slow to hold the curve, so return base_speed to 1.5 and keep kp at 1.5.
requested_changes: If runs stay on track with progress above 0.5: keep kp at 1.5 and kd at 0.6, and raise controller.base_speed in steps (1.3 to 1.5, then to 1.6) to recover finish time, since iteration 0 showed the 3 s limit needs about 1.5 m/s.

If the slalom still goes off track with steering_oscillation above 0.08: raise controller.kd from 0.6 toward 1.0 before changing kp, because iteration 0 showed oscillation of 0.10 to 0.14 that kd was meant to damp.

If runs go off track with low oscillation and progress stalled: return controller.base_speed to 1.5 and keep kp at 1.5, since the iteration 0 slalom failures came from overshoot and the 1.3 speed may be too slow to hold the curve.
